_comment: llama.cpp greedy references for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, recorded once: the
only oracle is a CPU-only build that prefills the 246 GB Q2_K file at
2.3 tok/s, so the 2049-token run costs about 15 minutes.
Reproduce from a clone of vcruz305/llama.cpp branch runtime/deepseek41
at 5210c7c, built CPU-only, with a passthrough chat template
('{{ messages[0]["content"] }}') so the prompt file is consumed
verbatim:
llama-cli -m <first shard> --chat-template-file passthrough.jinja
--single-turn -f <prompt> --temp 0 --top-k 1 --seed 0 -n <n_predict>
-c 4096 --no-display-prompt --no-warmup
This build has no -no-cnv; --single-turn replaces it.
Each prompt file is gmlx's OWN rendered V4.1 prompt, so a matching
prompt_tokens count also checks the bundled chat template.
gmlx itself is deterministic: the same settings twice give a bit-identical
logit vector (measured max|dlogit| 0.00000) and identical text. The forks
recorded below are between two PREFILL PATHS, each self-consistent: a
single pass over the prompt, and 16-token chunks through the cache.
Those paths are the same math - test_chunked_prefill_matches_one_pass holds
them to atol 2e-5 on a tiny model - so on 40 real layers they differ only by
float reassociation: max|dlogit| 2.36, mean 0.43. The logits are bfloat16,
whose ulp is 0.25 at these magnitudes, so that is about 2 ulps mean and 9
worst case. The argmax flips wherever the true top1-top2 gap is inside that
band, which free-form reasoning text hits often (0.25, one ulp, at the
measured position). The oracle adds its own kernels and reduction order on
top of the same effect.
So a greedy trajectory does not identify an implementation: it identifies a
path. The answer is what every path agrees on, so 'answer' is what the tests
assert and 'continuation' is recorded for diagnosis only.
